section_summary.extract_value: This Discussion section presents findings from a single study validating a Standard Chinese translation of the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2) across 154 men and 191 women. The study found that the one-dimensional BAS-2 model had adequate fit and was invariant across sex, with body appreciation significantly associated with life satisfaction, self-esteem, and in women only, with weight discrepancy and BMI. The authors note that while their findings differ from some previous studies showing higher BAS-2 scores in men, the effect sizes were small, and they suggest the Standard Chinese BAS-2 opens possibilities for cross-cultural comparisons of body appreciation.

section_summary.extract_value: This section presents findings from a confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) of the Standard Chinese translation of the Body Appreciation Scale-2 (BAS-2). The study found that a one-dimensional model with all items loading onto a single factor had adequate fit, consistent with the parent model and translations in other languages (Cantonese and Persian). Body appreciation scores showed good internal consistency and convergent validity, with significant associations to life satisfaction, self-esteem, and in women only, weight discrepancy and BMI. The CFA results also demonstrated that the one-dimensional model was invariant across sex, with no significant differences in body appreciation scores between women and men.
